entries.target: wine:Domaine Coudert ‘Clos de la Roilette’ Fleurie 2023
entries.value: Domaine Coudert Clos de la Roilette Fleurie 2023 is Gamay from a walled vineyard the Coudert family farm where Fleurie, a Beaujolais cru, meets Moulin-à-Vent. Farmed and made by the family to drink young, it gives red cherry, raspberry and violet, light, soft and fresh. Low tannin will not turn bitter against the tasso and Creole sauce of the New Orleans Shrimp & Grits, and bright fruit lifts the raw beef of the Steak Tartare with Rye: our value bottle for both. We serve it lightly chilled, 55 to 58°F, in a Burgundy bowl, never decanted. The clos gives a firmer, darker Fleurie than the cru usually makes.

entries.value: Domaine Faiveley Bourgogne Rouge 2022 is Pinot Noir under Burgundy’s regional name, from a family house in Nuits-Saint-Georges. Bottled as plain Bourgogne rather than under one village, it shows the grape before any single place: bright cherry and red currant, light to medium body, fresh acidity and fine tannin. With the Roasted Rohan Duck Breast, our value bottle, the acidity trims the rich meat while the red fruit echoes the glazed peaches. We serve it at 57 to 60°F in a Burgundy bowl, opened at the table, no decanting. Faiveley, founded in 1825, farms vines from Mercurey in the Côte Chalonnaise up to the Grand Crus of Chambertin.

entries.value: Marcel Lapierre Morgon 2023 is cru Beaujolais, Gamay from the family’s old vines at Villié-Morgon. It ferments in whole bunches with native yeasts and little or no added sulphur, giving crushed strawberry, cherry and a floral lift, silky, with very low tannin and bright acidity. With so little tannin, the soft-boiled egg and hollandaise of the Eggs Owen stay sweet while the fruit meets the red wine-braised short rib débris: our value bottle for that plate. We pour it lightly chilled, 55 to 59°F, in a Burgundy bowl, never decanted. The late Marcel Lapierre led Beaujolais back to natural winemaking, and his children run the estate now.

entries.value: Jean Foillard Côte du Py Morgon 2022 is Gamay grown on the hill at the centre of Morgon, its decomposed schist unlike the granite of other crus. It ferments long and cool in whole bunches with native yeasts and rests in old Burgundy barrels. Dark cherry, plum and violet carry a stony, savoury edge, deeper than the usual Beaujolais, and soft tannin meets the tasso, Creole sauce and pimento cheese grit cake: our classic bottle for the New Orleans Shrimp & Grits. We serve it at 57 to 60°F in a Burgundy bowl, no decanting. An old local verb, morgonner, names a Morgon that has aged into kirsch and earth.

entries.value: Domaine Jean Grivot Les Charmois Nuits-Saint-Georges 2013 is Pinot Noir from a village vineyard south of the town, made by a family domaine in Vosne-Romanée and aged about eighteen months in French oak. At thirteen years its red cherry has dried, with forest floor and mushroom, silky tannin and fresh acidity. Those earthy notes answer the preserved shiitakes and rice grits of the Blackened Tofu, and the gentle tannin stays calm under the spice: our classic bottle for the tofu. We serve it at 58 to 62°F in a Burgundy bowl, poured slowly, decanted only for sediment. The family’s range climbs from village wines like this to Richebourg.

At ten years it gives dark cherry, plum, earth and spice, the structure easing into a long, savoury finish. We open it twenty to thirty minutes ahead and pour at 60 to 63°F in a Burgundy bowl. Henri Gouges helped lead Burgundy to estate bottling.

entries.target: wine:Domaine Joseph Drouhin ‘Clos des Mouches’ Beaune Premier Cru 2015
entries.value: Domaine Joseph Drouhin Clos des Mouches Beaune Premier Cru 2015 is Pinot Noir grown on the slope above Beaune, where the Drouhin house owns more of the clos than anyone. It is farmed organically and biodynamically and raised with modest new oak, for elegance over weight. Eleven years on, red and black cherry meet rose and spice, silky and long, for roast poultry, veal, mushrooms and a guest who wants perfume over power. We serve it at 58 to 62°F in a Burgundy bowl, no decanting, and let it open in the glass. Joseph Drouhin founded the house in 1880, and it makes the clos in red and white.
